proposed_widenings.name: on_received_hit_window
proposed_widenings.justification: Fire Shield deals retaliatory damage to any attacker who lands a melee hit on the caster. This requires a window that opens when the caster *receives* a melee attack hit — the inverse of the existing on_hit_window (which fires when the caster lands a hit). No v4 atom covers this direction.
proposed_widenings.evidence: whenever a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack roll, the shield erupts with flame. The attacker takes 2d8 Fire damage from a warm shield or 2d8 Cold damage from a chill shield.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_resistance (OngoingOperation variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: Fire Shield grants the caster Resistance to Cold or Fire damage for the spell's duration. The v4 atom grant_resistance exists, but OngoingOperation in types.ts only has roll_modifier and damage_on_hit — no grant_resistance variant. The resistance is the other half of the spell's persistent effect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The warm shield grants you Resistance to Cold damage, and the chill shield grants you Resistance to Fire damage.

proposed_widenings.name: retaliatory_damage (OngoingOperation or EffectTarget variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: The retaliatory damage targets the attacker (not the caster, not a designated target). The existing damage effect atom targets within the attachment scope. A retaliatory damage operation needs to express that the damage target is the creature that triggered the on_received_hit_window, which is directionally opposite to the normal attachment flow.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The attacker takes 2d8 Fire damage from a warm shield or 2d8 Cold damage from a chill shield.

notes: Fire Shield has two independently un-encodable mechanics. (1) The resistance grant requires a new OngoingOperation variant; grant_resistance exists in the v4 atom taxonomy but is absent from types.ts OngoingOperation. (2) The retaliatory damage requires a new window atom (on_received_hit_window) that fires when the caster receives a melee hit — the inverse of on_hit_window. Both widenings are independent pressures. The binary warm/chill choice (selecting resistance type + retaliation damage type at cast time) is a third authoring gap but is secondary once the above two are resolved. The 10-minute non-concentration timed duration is representable as-is.
